policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads a singular subject with a singular verb, 'what is seen hath not been made', against the plural 'things which appear' later in the same clause; the plural τά βλεπόμενα would have given 'the things which are seen have not been made'.

ASV 'God bearing witness in respect of his gifts' makes θεοῦ the genitive subject of the participle μαρτυροῦντος; the dative τῷ θεῷ would attach to the gifts ('his gifts to God'), which ASV does not render. The 'somewhat uncertain' note is classed other and reports uncertainty without naming a reading.
ASV 'he being dead yet speaketh' is active; the passive λαλεῖται would give 'is yet spoken of'.

ASV 'before his translation' supplies the possessive that English idiom requires for a bare μεταθέσεως as readily as it renders an explicit αὐτοῦ, and 'his' is not italicized either way; the English does not distinguish.
The variant is the article before the proper name Ἀβραάμ, which English does not render; ASV 'By faith Abraham' is identical under either reading.
ASV 'to go out unto a place which he was to receive' is indefinite, matching anarthrous τόπον; the articular τὸν τόπον would have given 'the place'.

ASV makes Sarah the subject — 'even Sarah herself received power' — which requires the nominative αὐτὴ Σάρρα, not the dative αὐτῇ Σάρρᾳ construing with Abraham; and ASV renders no 'barren', excluding στεῖρα.
ASV ends the clause at 'when she was past age' and renders no 'and she bore a child', so ἔτεκεν is absent.
λαβόντες and κομισάμενοι both yield ASV 'not having received the promises'; the English does not distinguish them. The mapped note is a greek_gloss on 'according to' and bears on another word.
ASV 'if indeed they had been mindful' is past, rendering the imperfect ἐμνημόνευον in an unreal condition; the present μνημονεύουσιν would have given 'if they are mindful'.
ἐξέβησαν and ἐξῆλθον are both rendered 'they went out'; ASV's wording does not distinguish the two aorists.
ASV renders the conjunction — 'even concerning things to come' — which the omission would leave nothing to translate.
ASV 'as by dry land' translates ξηρά, which alone conventionally means dry land, so 'land' is no evidence that γῆς stood in the text; the English is the same under either reading.
The variant is verb number with the neuter plural subject τὰ τείχη; ASV 'the walls of Jericho fell down' is identical whether the Greek verb is plural or singular.
The variant is the order of με and γάρ, which English word order does not preserve; ASV 'for the time will fail me' fits either.

ASV lists 'Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah' with no conjunctions, matching the asyndeton of the base; the RP reading's τε καί and καί would have surfaced as 'and Samson, and Jephthah', as ASV does render the later 'David and Samuel and the prophets'.
μαχαίρης and μαχαίρας are declensional variants of the same noun; ASV 'the edge of the sword' does not distinguish them.
ἐδυναμώθησαν and its compound ἐνεδυναμώθησαν both give ASV 'from weakness were made strong'; the English does not distinguish.

ASV renders both verbs and in the order 'they were sawn asunder, they were tempted', which is ἐπρίσθησαν ἐπειράσθησαν; the base omits ἐπειράσθησαν and the WH order would have given 'tempted' before 'sawn asunder'.
μαχαίρης and μαχαίρας are declensional variants of the same noun; ASV 'slain with the sword' does not distinguish them.
ASV 'wandering in deserts and mountains' renders either preposition as 'in'; the English does not distinguish ἐπί from ἐν here.
ASV 'And these all, having had witness borne to them' renders the demonstrative οὗτοι; without it the text would read only 'And all'.
